schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE INSURANCE (
    PID INT,
    TIV_2015 NUMERIC,
    TIV_2016 NUMERIC,
    LAT NUMERIC,
    LON NUMERIC,
    PRIMARY KEY (PID),
    CHECK (TIV_2015 >= 0),
    CHECK (TIV_2016 >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2: SELECT SUM(TIV_2016) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE CONCAT(LON, LAT) IN (SELECT CONCAT(LON, LAT) FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LON, LAT HAVING COUNT(*) = 1) AND TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT SUM(TIV_2016) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE CONCAT(LON, LAT) IN (SELECT CONCAT(LON, LAT) FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LON, LAT HAVING COUNT(*) = 1) AND TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)
counterexample: INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (1, 100, 200, 1.1, 2.2); INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (2, 100, 300, 1.1, 2.2);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they use different methods to identify unique locations. Q1 uses the (LAT, LON) pair directly, while Q2 concatenates LON and LAT into a single string. This can lead to different results if LAT and LON are not unique when considered as separate values.
